title: Cap. 6 Arg. 8 Primo: Augustine—some not called; media withheld by the abyss of predestination
pass_a_gloss: First we will bring forward those testimonies which deny that the grace of evangelical preaching, Christ's death being supposed, is owed or given to all—indeed affirm that it is denied to some, and that from the purpose of the divine will: which would never happen if grace were owed to all in order to the death of Christ. Augustine, On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 8: From two impious persons grown in age, why this one is so called that he follows the one calling, but that one is either not called or not so called—the judgments of God are inscrutable. Here he openly acknowledges that some are not called at all. And chapter 14 teaches that to certain ones who by God's higher judgment have not been separated from the mass of perdition, those means are not applied by which they could believe. In both places he asserts the negation of the means, and refers it to the inscrutable abyss of divine predestination, not to disparities of human wills or actions, as the Pelagians and Semi-Pelagians were accustomed to do. See also chapter 11, where he refers to the will of God and hidden predestination the fact that God is unwilling to help certain ones.
pass_b_english: First, the Fathers who deny that—Christ's death granted—the grace of Gospel preaching is owed or given to all, and even say it is withheld from some by the purpose of God's will. That could not happen if grace were owed to everyone on the strength of Christ's death. Augustine, On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 8: take two ungodly adults—why is one called so that he follows the Caller, while the other is not called, or not called that way? God's judgments are inscrutable. He plainly owns that some are not called at all. Chapter 14 adds that for some not cut out of the mass of perdition by God's higher judgment, the means by which they could believe are simply not applied. In both places he affirms that the means are denied, and he traces it to the unsearchable depth of divine predestination—not to uneven human wills or works, the Pelagian and Semi-Pelagian habit. Chapter 11 says the same: God chooses not to help some, and that rests on his will and hidden predestination.
source_text: Primo illa afferemus quae gratiam Evangelicae praedicationis, supposita Christi morte, omnibus debitam aut datam negant, imo aliquibus negatam affirmant, idque ex proposito voluntatis Divinae: quod nunquam fieret, si omnibus gratia debita esset in ordine ad mortem Christi. Augustinus, De bono persever. cap. 8. Ex duobus aetate grandibus impiis, cur iste ita vocetur ut vocantem sequatur, ille autem aut non vocetur aut non ita vocetur, inscrutabilia sunt judicia Dei. Hic aperte agnoscit quosdam omnino non vocari. Et cap. 14. docet, quibusdam qui Dei altiori judicio a perditionis massa non sunt discreti, ea media non adhiberi per quae possent credere. Utroque in loco negationem mediorum asserit, et revocat ad inscrutabilem abyssum praedestinationis Divinae, non ad discrimina voluntatum aut actionum humanarum, sicut Pelagiani et Semipelagiani solebant. Vide etiam cap. 11. ubi ad voluntatem Dei et occultam praedestinationem refert, quod quibusdam Deus nolit subvenire.
